parameters.url: =https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{{ $('Validate input').first().json.owner }}/{{ $('Validate input').first().json.repo }}/HEAD/{{ $('Repo contents').all().map(i => i.json.name).find(n => n && n.toLowerCase() === 'dockerfile') || 'Dockerfile' }}

nodes.name: Repo dockerfile
nodes.notes: Resolves the Dockerfile's real filename from the repo listing - `dockerfile` is as valid as `Dockerfile` and a 404 here silently defaulted the port (Problem #143).

nodes.name: Ensure Nomad namespace
nodes.notes: Calls the Nomad Namespace Creator workflow by ID. This workflow holds NO Nomad management credential; the token lives only in the sub-workflow.

nodes.name: Repo manifest
nodes.notes: Reads the project manifest so the generator works from facts, not guesses. raw.githubusercontent.com does not spend the api.github.com rate budget.

nodes.name: Generate a Dockerfile
nodes.notes: Same model and credential as the platform classifier. It produces TEXT; every decision that follows is made from measured facts.

nodes.name: Check the generated Dockerfile
nodes.notes: Strips fences, requires a real FROM, reads EXPOSE for the port, and builds a Kaniko Job identical to the human-written path except for how the Dockerfile is delivered.

nodes.name: Start AI build
nodes.notes: Same sandbox as every other build in this lab.

nodes.name: Check AI build status
nodes.notes: The Job is bounded at 420s, so by now it has genuinely finished or failed.

nodes.name: Read the build error
nodes.notes: Finds the failed build pod so its log can be fed back to the model.

nodes.name: Read the build log
nodes.notes: The actual Kaniko error, so the retry can self-correct from evidence rather than guesswork.

nodes.name: Write the retry prompt
nodes.notes: Feeds the real Kaniko error back to the model. Exactly one retry - capped by construction, not by a counter that could drift.

nodes.name: Generate a Dockerfile (retry)
nodes.notes: Second and final generation attempt.

nodes.name: Check the retry Dockerfile
nodes.notes: Identical validation and sandbox to attempt 1 - written once, reused, so the two attempts cannot drift apart.

nodes.name: Which build won?
nodes.notes: Applies the built image to the SAME Deployment as the starter - a rolling update, so the working site is never taken down by the upgrade (Part 23 item 16).

nodes.name: Upgrade the site to the built image
Let the new pod come up
Point the Service at the built port

conditions.leftValue: ={{ $('Analyse repo').first().json.repoAnalysed && !$('Analyse repo').first().json.hasDockerfile && ($('Pick from fixed menu').first().json.choice === 'kubernetes' || $('Pick from fixed menu').first().json.choice === 'nomad') }}

nodes.name: Try an AI Dockerfile?
nodes.notes: Generates ONLY when the repo was actually read AND ships no Dockerfile (case-insensitive, #143). If the GitHub listing failed we cannot know, so we do not generate - a missing answer is not a negative one.

nodes.name: Worth a second try?
nodes.notes: A timeout is not a Dockerfile defect. Retrying one wastes the single retry and a build slot, and would very likely time out again for the same reason.

nodes.name: Build settled?
nodes.notes: Loops back to the wait until the Job has genuinely succeeded or failed. Capped at 35 passes by $runIndex so a check that errors every time cannot spin forever.

nodes.name: Retry settled?
nodes.notes: Loops back to the wait until the Job has genuinely succeeded or failed. Capped at 35 passes by $runIndex so a check that errors every time cannot spin forever.

nodes.name: Which platform won?
nodes.notes: The image is built the same way for both platforms; only how it is DEPLOYED differs.

nodes.name: Submit Nomad job (AI image)
nodes.notes: Replaces the http-echo starter with the tenant's own AI-built image, same job ID.

nodes.name: List AI allocations
nodes.notes: The list endpoint carries no AllocatedResources - the detail fetch below is required.

nodes.name: AI allocation placed?
nodes.notes: Polls until Nomad has actually allocated a port. Capped at 21 passes so a job that never places cannot spin forever.

nodes.name: Point Nomad at the AI image
nodes.notes: Re-applies only the EndpointSlice, with the port read from the new allocation.

nodes.name: Route Nomad to the AI image
Read the namespace
nodes.notes: Read back after create OR 409 - a 409 body carries no labels, so ownership can only be established by looking.

nodes.name: Is it ours to use?
nodes.notes: Fails CLOSED: an unreadable or unlabelled namespace is not treated as ours.

nodes.name: Ours?
nodes.notes: The refusal path exists so a name collision ends with an honest answer, never a deployment into someone else's namespace.

nodes.name: Let the repo pod come up
Point the Service at the repo port
